subject: Proposed amendment: 36-month term + seat scale (Orion Health)
messages:
From: markus_klein
To: Claire Jensen <cjensen@orionhealth.com>, Orion Health Legal <legal@orionhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett, sofia_ivanova
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed amendment: 36-month term + seat scale (Orion Health)

Claire / Orion legal team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a clean amendment + a proposed order form that rolls the current 24-month subscription forward to a 36-month term and adds the phased seat scale: +150 seats in month 1, +350 seats by month 12 (see OrderForm_0827.xlsx). Key commercial asks from your side I captured on the call: 1) amortized pricing for the additional seats across the extended term; 2) a one-time migration credit for the pilot overage; and 3) a narrower SLA credit definition for performance during phased onboarding.

From our side we recommended: a) convert the current SLA credit language into a table (attached SLA_Credit_Table.pdf) so the credit cap and trigger windows are explicit; b) a mutual indemnity carveout limited to IP claims arising from derivative training (we added proposed language in the amendment); and c) keep billing annual in arrears but allow a 90-day payment plan for the first-year uplift invoice.

I attached a redline (Orion_Amendment_v3_redline.docx) showing the changes to the MSA and an editable order form. Can you and legal confirm if the indemnity carveout, billing plan, and the SLA credit table are acceptable? Ideally we’d get an initial legal marker by Fri 24 Sept so we can route the final for signature the week of Sep 27.

If helpful I can loop in CS to outline the phased onboarding milestones tied to the seat adds.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Orion_Amendment_v3_redline.docx (document), OrderForm_0827.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_Credit_Table.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett
To: markus_klein, sofia_ivanova
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment: 36-month term + seat scale (Orion Health)

Markus — quick internal notes before we get back to Claire.

I read the redline. Two asks from Legal/RevOps that we should 1) pre-clear before external push:
- Indemnity: tighten the mutual indemnity carveout wording so it only applies to claims "directly arising from use of the Service"; avoid broad "derivative training" language that could be read as excluding our standard data protections.
- SLA credits: reduce the total cap on credits for the first 6 months of the onboarding phase (we can offer higher caps after month 6). Use the SLA_Credit_Table as the external-facing artifact, but mark the first-row credit cap as conditional on remedial plan acceptance.

Commercial ops items:
- Billing: annual in arrears is fine, but we should not extend a 90-day plan beyond year 1. If they insist, propose a 60-day plan + 1% finance fee.
- Pricing: for the seat uplift propose a blended rate for the first 12 months (to smooth their AR), then standard list rate thereafter. Add a short example calc in the order form.

Sofia — can you draft the short clause tightening the indemnity and send me a clean paragraph to attach to the next external email?

Markus — once we have the tightened language I'll review, then we can propose the compromise on credits/billing.

Laura Bennett
Director, Renewals & Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Markus / Laura / Sofia —

Thanks for the update and the attachments. Legal reviewed Orion_Amendment_v3_redline.docx and we put a parallel redline in track changes with three primary items: 1) limit the indemnity carveout to not apply to Orion's regulatory obligations (we cannot accept language that could be read to prevent our compliance-driven data-sharing duties); 2) ask for a 30-day credit remittance timeline (we prefer quicker operational resolution); and 3) request a short-lived price protection guarantee for the first 12 months of the uplift (to protect against any mid-term list increases).

I attached our markup (forwarded as Orion_Legal_v2_trackchanges.docx) to this thread. Brian in our procurement team asked if Redwood can accept DocuSign routing with two Orion signatories (Legal + Procurement) and a single Redwood signer. If we can get a revised amendment by end of day Sep 24, Orion will target a signature window the week of Sep 27.

One open question: the billing cadence for the uplift — procurement asked for annual invoicing but staggered payment schedules across the first year. If Redwood wants annual in arrears, can you confirm you can support split payments inside our AR system (we can accept two invoices tied to the same order form).

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

Regards,
Claire Jensen
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Orion Health
cjensen@orionhealth.com | +1 212-555-0199
